INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE OCTOBER 5, 2020
  OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUISNESS IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT MEETING

The Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District meeting will be closed to the public in
compliance with Governor Newsom’s Executive Order to minimize the spread of the COVID-
19 Virus. Additionally, the meeting will be conducted via teleconference with members
participating remotely. Considering this, the customary meeting format has been modified.
Even with this change in format, the City is still encouraging public participation and wishes to
make residents aware of the following opportunities for participation:

  1) View the meeting through the City’s website at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream

  2) Please submit your written comments via email at planning@cityoflaverne.org. They
  will be shared with the District Board Members prior to the meeting and will be made
  part of the permanent record. We ask that you provide those emails before 7:00 p.m.
  the day before the meeting.

  3) For individuals that wish to share their comments during the live stream, you may
  email planning@cityoflaverne.org by 7:00 a.m. on the day of the meeting with a phone
  number and the item(s) you wish to speak on. We will call you back at the appropriate
  time during the meeting for your comment.
   AGENDA

  Advisory Board

  Tuesday, October 5, 2020 – 8:30 am –

   OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTIRICT
  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Monday, August 3, 2020

1.  The teleconference meeting was called to order by Chairperson Craig Walters at 8:31
  a.m. Mr. Walters stated that questions can be emailed to planning@cityoflaverne.org.

  Advisory Board Members present: Craig Walters, Chris Gendreau, Micky Rehm, Jason
  Miller, Marianne Stark and Matt Forgey. City Representatives present: Community
  Development Director Eric Scherer and Administrative Clerk Natalie Hiatt. Others
  present: Craig Hoelzel and Leah Skinner.

2.  CALENDAR

  Cool Cruise – Pending - Saturday, August 22nd

  Beer/Wine Walk – Pending - September 26th

  Mr. Scherer stated that a Public Comment was received from Jackson Salinas via email.

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES July 6, 2020 and July 13, 2020

  It was moved by Ms. Rehm and seconded by Mr. Miller to approve the minutes of July 6,
  2020 and July 13, 2020. Motion carried by a 5-0 vote.

4.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A.  Cool Cruise Car Show – Mr. Hoelzel contacted the Department of Health for
  approval. The Health Department considers the Car Show a gathering/event and is
  not allowed during the current State and Health Order.

  Mr. Scherer stated that the City has to follow county order and currently no
  gatherings of any size are allowed.

  Mr. Hoelzel needs only ten day notice to continue event and stated that he would
  like to hold out longer.

  Mr. Gendreau asked if the City would take down the closure for the event.

  Mr. Scherer stated that the car show would need to modified.

  Mr. Miller and Ms. Rehm both suggested moving the event to November.

  1
   It was moved by Mr. Miller and seconded by Ms. Stark to combine the Cool
  Cruise with the Holiday Cruise scheduled for November 21, 2020. Motion carried
  by a 5-0 vote.

  B.  Beer/Wine Walk – To be discussed at the Association meeting.

  C.  D Street Closure for Restaurants – Mr. Scherer stated that since the last meeting
  trees were added to the street and the public tables were removed.

  Ms. Rehm stated that on Sunday the trash cans were overflowing.

  Mr. Scherer stated that Public Works is not staffed on Sundays.

  Ms. Rehm volunteered to email the restaurants requesting their help. She also
  suggested that the employees park in Lot E.

  D.  ULV Crawl Update – Event cancelled. Mr. Miller stated that the University would
  be remote online for the fall with limited staff on campus. Only housing a handful
  of students that require housing.

  E.  Business Assistance Grants – Mr. Scherer stated there are a lot of available funds.
  Approximately 40 applications are currently pending.

5.  COMMITTEE REPORTS/ UPDATES

  A.  City Report (Eric Scherer): None

  B.  University Report (Jason Miller): None

  C.  Marketing (Micky Rehm): None

  D.  Chamber Report (Leah Skinner): Ms. Skinner announced on August 13th the
  Chamber and College of Law will discuss employment, workers compensation,
  and tenants’ rights.

  E.  Social Media Update (Micky Rehm): None

  F.  Financial Report: None

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT (Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be
  deferred to the following meeting, as required by California Brown Act Law)

  Public Comments received from Gus Moran and Jackson Salinas via email.

7.  ADJOURNMENT

  2
 Meeting was adjourned at 9:18 a.m., to the next meeting to be held on Monday,
September 14, 2020 at 8:30 a.m.

Respectively submitted,

_____________________
Natalie M. Hiatt

Hi city of La Verne,
My name is Gus Moran and I am a local resident and professional chalk artist. I am a graduate of

I would like permission to chalk a mural on D street where out door dining is currently being

and my hope is that I hear a positive response from the council, thank you for your

Gus Moran

   OLD TOWN LA VERNE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTIRICT
  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Monday, September 8, 2020

1.  The teleconference meeting was called to order by Chairperson Craig Walters at 8:33
  a.m. Mr. Walters stated that questions can be emailed to planning@cityoflaverne.org.

  Advisory Board Members present: Craig Walters, Chris Gendreau, Micky Rehm,
  Marianne Stark and Matt Forgey. City Representatives present: Community
  Development Director Eric Scherer and Administrative Clerk Natalie Hiatt. Police
  Department Staff present: Chief Nick Paz, Captain Colleen Flores, and Community
  Services Officer Hollie Savage. Others present: Larry Pirkle of University of La Verne
  and Leah Skinner of the Chamber of Commerce.

2.  CALENDAR

  Car Show – Saturday, November 21, 2020

  Halloween Coloring Contest – September 10th-October 8th

  Mr. Scherer stated that the coloring contest submittals can be done through the online
  portal or in person at City Hall.

  Mr. Scherer stated that a Public Comment was received from Jackson Salinas via e-mail.

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  N/A

4.  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Police Department Business Watch Program - Officer Savage announced a new
  program and partnership between the Police Department and merchants. She
  stated there are 4-5 officers working at one time and 1,300 businesses within the
  City. The program encourages businesses to call if something looks suspicious
  and to lookout for fellow merchants. More program information is available on
  the Police Department website.

  Ms. Stark asked how the Board Members can help with the program.

  Officer Savage stated sharing by word of mouth and with social media.

5.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A.  D Street Closure for Restaurants - Mr. Scherer stated that the City would continue
  with the closure as long as the Board is in support.
  1
   Ms. Skinner stated that the street closure has helped keep the businesses alive.

  Mr. Forgey has noticed a lot more traffic on Third Street including speeding
  vehicles, skateboarders, and smoking.

  Mr. Walters stated that he also noticed the skateboarders and bicyclists. He is also
  concerned about the crowded sidewalks. He asked if the University had any
  concerns for continued use of their parking lot.

  Mr. Pirkle had no concerns.

  Mr. Forgey requested “No Skateboarding” and “No Smoking” signs.

  Mr. Walters asked Mr. Scherer to address the petition received to keep the street
  permanently closed.

  Mr. Scherer stated that the request has not been presented to council.

  B.  Car Show – November Date - Mr. Scherer stated that the Car Show is scheduled
  for November 21st the Saturday before Thanksgiving. The event will take place as
  long as the current County order is lifted.

  Mr. Gendreau asked if the Christmas tree will be delivered before the car show.

  Ms. Rehm stated that the tree is not available until the following week.

  Mr. Scherer stated that money is set aside for a tree decorator.

  Ms. Rehm will ask the tree vendor if the tree can be delivered early. She also
  stated that she will contact the decorator from last year and Joann Lammens of
  Gina T. to check their availability.

6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS/ UPDATES

  A.  City Report (Eric Scherer): None

  B.  University Report (Jason Miller): Mr. Pirkle announced that online classes have
  started. Currently there are 150 students living at the dorms and essential
  employees are on campus. Regular testing, HVAC updates, plexiglass, reduced
  class sizes, and washing stations will be provided. He stated that the Brown
  property on Arrow Highway will be removed down to the slab.

  Ms. Rehm asked if the Lot E can be used for employee parking on a more
  permanent basis.

  2
   Ms. Stark also suggested directing employees to park in the lot behind the Public
  Safety building.

  Mr. Scherer recommends tabling for further discussion next month.

  C.  Marketing (Micky Rehm): Ms. Rehm announced a new business will be in the
  space previously occupied by Serendipity.

  D.  Chamber Report (Leah Skinner): Ms. Skinner announced the Bonita Unified
  School District forum to be held Tuesday, October 20th.

  E.  Social Media Update (Micky Rehm): None

  F.  Financial Report: None

7.  PUBLIC COMMENT (Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be
  deferred to the following meeting, as required by California Brown Act Law)

  Public Comment received from Jackson Salinas via e-mail.

8.  ADJOURNMENT

  Meeting was adjourned at 9:28 a.m., to the next meeting to be held on Monday, October
  5, 2020 at 8:30 a.m.

  Respectively submitted,

  _____________________
  Natalie M. Hiatt

minutes_text:
OLD TOWN LA VERIIE BUSINESS IMPROVEMENT DISTIRICT
  MINTITES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  Monday, October 5,2020

I  The teleconference meeting was called to order by Chairperson Craig Walters at8:32a.m
  Mr. Walters stated that questions can be emailed to plannins@cityoflaverne.ore.

  Advisory Board Members present: Craig Walters, Chris Gendreau, Jason Miller, Matt
  Forgey and Micky Rehm (arrived late). City Representatives present: Mayor Tim
  Hepburn, Community Development Director Eric Scherer and Administrative Clerk
  Natalie Hiatt. Others present: Craig Hoelzel.

2.  CALENDAR

  Car Show - Saturday, November 21,2020
  Mr. Scherer stated large events are still not allowed and it is unlikely for the event to
  occur under today's guidelines.

  Mayor Hepburn stated that he will continue to make contact with the County
  Supervisor's Office.

  Mr. Hoelzel stated that he needs two week notice to cancel the event. He asked the board
  to hold offon cancelling the event untilNovember 2nd'

  It was moved by Mr. Gendreau and seconded by Mr. Miller to hold off on further
  discussion until the November 2nd meeting. Motion carried by a 4-0 vote (Ms. Rehm was
  not present for the vote).

  Halloween Coloring Contest - September l0th-October 8n
  Mr. Scherer stated that the coloring contest application is available online. The entries
  will be posted in the windows of the downtown businesses.

  Mr. Gendreau asked what should be done if there are trick-or-treaters on Halloween.

  Mr. Scherer stated that the County backed off on their position of prohibiting trick-or-
  treating but they do not recommend it. lf a business or home wishes to provide candy
  they may do so at their discretion. The City will be releasing information later this week
  regarding two Halloween programs being organized by the Community Services
  Department.

3  APPROVAL OF MINUTES - August 3,2020 and September 8,2020

  Public Comment was received from Jackson Salinas via e-mail.

  It was moved by Mr. Gendreau and seconded by Mr. Miller to approve the minutes with a

  I
   correction to the public comment. Motion carried by a 4-0 vote (Ms. Rehm was not
  present for the vote).

4.  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Merchant Parking Discussion - Ms. Rehm stated that she emailed the businesses
  and received no responses. She spoke to George Henderson about possibly
  utilizing the University parking lot for Downtown employee parking.

  Mr. Gendreau asked if the City is writing a letter regarding parking.

  Mr, Scherer stated a letter will be sent. Mr. Scherer reviewed the previous parking
  analysis and the consultant recommended not allowing employees to park in 90
  minute parking spots.

  Mr. Miller stated that Lot F at the University is also available for parking.

  Mr. Scherer will encourage business owners and employees to park in Lots E and
  F.

  B.  Discussion on Upcoming Events - Mr. Scherer stated that as of now it does not
  look like the County will allow events like the Holiday Stroll. He asked Ms.
  Rehm if the post card is still being mailed.

  Ms. Rehm stated that the post card should be sent even if the Holiday Stroll does
  not take place.

  Public Comment received from Jackson Salinas via email.

  Chairperson Walters stated that the post card will be further discussed at the
  Association meeting.

  C  Anticipated Board Changes - Mr. Gendreau stated that he will still be able to
  serve on the board through January 2021.

  Chairperson Walters asked that the City appoint a new alternate and make Matt
  Forgey a board member.

  Mr. Scherer stated that he will include notice of the open alternate position and an
  application in the parking letter.

  Public Comment received from Jackson Salinas via email'

  It was moved by Mr.Miller and seconded by Ms. Rehm to recommend the move
  of Mr. Forgey fiom alternate to full-time board member. Motion carried by a 4-0
  vote.

  2
 5.  CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A.  D Street Closure for Restaurants - Mr. Scherer stated that the city has made no
  changes to the set-up since the last meeting.

  Mayor Hepburn stated that in his personal opinion 50-60% occupancy is needed
  before D Street can be opened. He stated that people feel safer outdoors.

  Chairperson Walters asked if heaters and tenting with side walls will be allowed.

  Mr. Scherer stated that significant upgrades to the tenting are needed to allow for
  heaters in order to meet the Fire Department's rules and regulations.

  Ms. Rehm was concemed about having the street closed if the businesses do not
  utilize outdoor dining during the cold weather.

  Public Comment received by Jackson Salinas via e-mail.

  Mr. Scherer asked the board if they wanted to address the Public Comments
  received by Jackson Salinas.

  Mr. Gendreau stated that the Board will not disregard County and Governor
  Order.

  Mayor Hepbum stated we are doing well following the guidelines and we need to
  prepare for the change in weather.

  Chairperson Walters addressed the comment regarding the Board's ability to plan
  a political event for Major Williams.

  Mr. Scherer stated that this is a non-political board and cannot endorse any one
  candidate for seat or office. The only involvement the board has is hosting a
  candidate's forum for City Council elections.

6.  COMMITTEE REPORTS/ UPDATES

  A.  City Report (Eric Scherer): None

  B.  University Report (Jason Miller): Mr. Miller stated that the winter term will be
  remote. Enrollment is up this school year due to an increase in marketing last
  year.

  C.  Marketing (Micky Rehm): None

  D  Chamber Report (Leah Skinner): Mr. Scherer stated the La Verne and San Dimas
  Chambers will host the Bonita Unified School Board forum on Tuesday, October
  2oth 6:oop.m.

  J
   La Verne Restaurant Week will be October 2l-25th in place of the Taste of La
  Verne. Participating restaurants will offer specials during the event.

  E.  Social Media Update (Micky Rehm): Ms. Rehm encouraged everyone to support
  all business posts on social media and tag the Old Town page.

  F.  Financial Report: None

7  PUBLIC COMMENT (Any discussion or action on non-agendized items must be
  deferred to the following meeting, as required by California Brown Act Law)

  Public Comment received from Jackson Salinas via e-mail

8.  ADJOIIRNMENT

  Meeting was adjourned at 9: l8 a.m., to the next meeting to be held on Monday,
  November 3,2020 at 8:30 a.m.

  Hiatt
